25.0.0.en: Several years after the death of Sarah, Abraham married a concubine named Keturah and had six sons by her, and they in turn bore grandsons, some during Abraham's lifetime and others perhaps after his death. Despite the multitude of offspring that came from her, she added nothing to Abraham's life, but it was a human need, one that one wishes he had not had; yet the Holy Bible shows the great men of faith with all their weaknesses. Although he had been content with Sarah throughout his life, he became weak in his old age and needed to marry one of his maidservants. As for his marriage to his maidservant Hagar during Sarah's lifetime, it was not out of desire or need but to please Sarah and a mistaken attempt to carry out God's promise.

25.0.1.en: May you walk in self-restraint throughout your life, not only in marriage but in food, clothing and possessions, for the more you give them up, the more your heart is freed and is satisfied with God.

25.1.0.en: The concubines: the maidservants whom Abraham married, namely Hagar and Keturah.

25.1.1.en: The east country: the Arabian Peninsula and southern Iraq.

25.1.2.en: Abraham remembered God's word about sending Ishmael away and giving the inheritance to Isaac alone, so he gave gifts to his sons by Keturah and sent them away, and they went east, and Isaac remained alone in Canaan. He thus became Abraham's only heir, not only in material gifts but rather in faith and the love of God. This is a type of the inheritance of the Kingdom, which Christ gave to His Church, which alone received the glad tidings of Him.

25.2.0.en: Abraham lived in faith and in a righteous life pleasing to God throughout his life, and died at the age of 175. He had gone out from Haran, which lies between the Tigris and the Euphrates rivers, at the age of 75 and gone to Canaan; then he fathered Ishmael at the age of 86, and after that he fathered Isaac at the age of one hundred; Sarah died when he had reached 137; when Jacob and Esau were born he was 160; and at his death Ishmael had reached 89 years and Isaac 75 years, while Isaac's sons, Jacob and Esau, were 15 years old.

25.3.0.en: When Abraham died, all his neighbors heard of it. Ishmael was living near Mamre, where Abraham died, and perhaps Isaac sent for him, so he came and joined him in burying him in the cave of Machpelah beside Sarah. As for Abraham's sons by Keturah, they lived far away and did not attend the burial of their father.

25.4.0.en: Isaac lived at Beer-lahai-roi, where the angel appeared to Hagar (ch. 16:14), and lived in the faith of his father Abraham. He took care to live in this blessed place where the angel of God had appeared, and God blessed him spiritually and materially.

25.4.1.en: Take care to cling to spiritual places and spiritual people, so that this may help you to remember God and be encouraged on His way, and not be carried along with the current of the world and its dazzling means of advertising, so that God may bless you and appear always in your life.

25.4.2.en: We note that Abraham is a type of Christ in the following:

25.4.3.en: 1- Abraham left his family and his kindred in Ur of the Chaldees and obeyed God, and Christ left His glory in heaven and humbled Himself, becoming incarnate, in obedience to the Father.

25.4.4.en: 2- Abraham lived throughout his life detached, in a tent, and owned nothing but a tomb, and Christ lived poor, having nowhere to lay His head, even to death, the death of the Cross.

25.4.5.en: 3- Abraham built an altar in every place he went to and offered sacrifices, and Christ lifted up His prayer to the Father and offered Himself as a sacrifice of love on the Cross.

25.4.6.en: 4- Abraham fled to Egypt and blessed it, and Christ fled to Egypt and blessed it.

25.4.7.en: 5- Abraham triumphed over Chedorlaomer and all who were with him and brought back the captives, and Christ triumphed over Satan and bound him on the Cross, and brought out those held captive in Hades and raised them up to Paradise.

25.4.8.en: 6- Abraham obeyed God and offered the dearest thing he had, Isaac his beloved son, as a sacrifice, and Christ obeyed the Father and offered His life on the Cross.

25.4.9.en: We can summarize the life of our father Abraham in the following points:

25.4.10.en: 1- God's call to Abraham and his going out from Ur of the Chaldees with his wife Sarai, his father Terah and his brother's son Lot, and their going to Haran (ch. 11:31), (Acts 7:2).

25.4.11.en: 2- God called Abraham a second time, and he went out from Haran and went to Canaan, and He promised him blessing. (ch. 12:1)

25.4.15.en: 6- His victory over Chedorlaomer and the bringing back of the captives. (ch. 14)

25.4.17.en: 8- God's appearance to him and His confirmation of the promise to him. (ch. 15)

25.4.18.en: 9- His marriage to Hagar and the birth of Ishmael. (ch. 16)

25.4.19.en: 10- God's covenant with him when He appeared to him among the divided animals, and His giving him the covenant of circumcision. (ch. 17)

25.4.20.en: 11- God and the two angels as his guests, and the promise of Isaac. (ch. 18)

25.4.21.en: 12- His intercession for Sodom and Gomorrah. (ch. 18)

25.4.23.en: 14- The birth of Isaac, his weaning, and the casting out of Hagar and Ishmael. (ch. 21)

25.4.24.en: 15- His offering of Isaac as a sacrifice. (ch. 22)

25.4.25.en: 16- The death of his wife Sarah. (ch. 23)

25.4.26.en: 17- The choosing of Rebekah as a wife for his son Isaac. (ch. 24)

25.4.27.en: 18- His death and burial in the cave of Machpelah. (ch. 25)

25.5.0.en: Ishmael fathered 12 sons, whom the Holy Bible lists in order according to the years of their birth. They became chiefs of tribes that lived in the Arabian Peninsula, and some of them extended northward as far as Damascus and Iraq and took possession of the lands there and had many cattle, because God blessed them in number and possessions as He had promised Abraham, for they are his offspring, even if they did not live attached to him so as to live in his faith. Some of them formed famous tribes, such as Nebajoth, from whom came the Nabateans mentioned in the First Book of Maccabees (1 Macc 5:25; 9:35), who lived in the region between the Gulf of Aqaba and the Euphrates. Also Kedar, whose name means black, and whose tribe is mentioned in (Song 1:5), and from him came Geshem the Arabian who opposed Nehemiah (Neh 2:19), and from him the tribe of Quraysh came forth.

25.6.0.en: Havilah: it lies west of the Persian Gulf.

25.6.1.en: Shur: it lies southwest of Palestine.

25.6.2.en: Asshur: it includes all the lands from the Mediterranean Sea to the east of the Tigris River.

25.6.3.en: Ishmael, with his various tribes, lived in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, and some of his tribes extended into the region of Syria and Palestine. Ishmael lived to the age of 137 and then died.

25.6.4.en: If God blesses you and gives you material good things or offspring of renown, do not be preoccupied by this away from God, but use it to reach Him and thank Him for His blessings, for the aim of all God's gifts is to bind your heart to Him, so that you may enjoy a living faith and have a place in heaven.

25.7.s.en: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

25.7.0.en: Padan-aram: the plain between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, now called the land of the Jazirah, and Aram was one of the descendants of Shem.

25.7.1.en: Isaac married, at the age of 40, Rebekah the daughter of Bethuel and sister of Laban, who lived in Padan-aram, and Eliezer of Damascus brought her to Canaan.

25.8.0.en: Rebekah remained barren for 20 years, and Isaac's faith was not shaken, but he continued to pray, confident of God's promise, until she conceived.

25.8.1.en: Hold fast to the promises of God, who keeps you in all your ways and blesses your life, and be persistent with Him in prayer however long the time, that He may solve your problems, for He waits for the right time and gives you an opportunity for your faith to grow, but He never forgets you.

25.9.0.en: Why am I thus: she was distressed by the pains of the movement of the babes and came near to death, so a feeling of despair attacked her and she said, why is my life, which is an expression of her distress at the severity of the pain.

25.9.1.en: She went to inquire of the Lord: she lifted up her heart in prayer, or went to the altar that her husband Isaac had built and prayed to God.

25.9.2.en: The time of delivery drew near, and Rebekah felt a crowding or struggle in her womb and suffered much, and in the extremity of her distress she hastened to God, asking Him to deliver her from these pains, perhaps fearing that she would die or that the one in her womb would die.

25.10.0.en: Since her prayer was fervent, God reassured her and told her that she would give birth in peace and that she and the one in her womb would live; indeed He gave her the good news that she would bear two sons, each of whom would become a great people, and He also informed her that the offspring of the elder son would be enslaved to the offspring of the younger son. By this He means God's blessing upon the offspring of Jacob, who came to the Promised Land and killed the wicked original inhabitants of the land and took possession of their land.

25.11.0.en: Esau: the name means rough or hairy, and he was surnamed Edom, that is, red.

25.11.1.en: At the birth a red child came out of her womb, and they called him Esau, and his body was covered with hair. Then the second son came out holding the heel of his brother, and they called him Jacob, that is, he holds, because he took hold of his heel. Rebekah rejoiced, and so did Isaac, who was then sixty years old.

25.12.0.en: The two boys grew and became young men. Esau worked at hunting wild beasts and lived in a moving tent in the wilderness, searching for the wild animals that abound in these regions in order to hunt them. As for Jacob, he worked at shepherding sheep and also lived in a tent, and was distinguished by meekness and a life of faith, so the Holy Bible called him perfect for his care for the spiritual life.

25.13.0.en: Isaac felt Esau's strength, which appeared in his courage and his hunting of wild beasts, so he loved him and preferred him to Jacob. But Rebekah the mother loved Jacob because of his righteousness and meekness and preferred him to Esau.

25.14.0.en: Esau went out on a hunting trip in which he exerted great effort running after the wild beasts, and when he returned to his tent very weary, he found his brother Jacob, who was then living next to him, cooking red lentils, that is, yellow tending toward red, and its smell was pleasant, while Esau was in great fatigue and hunger.

25.15.0.en: When Esau smelled the lentils and saw them with his eyes, he longed to eat of them and asked his brother Jacob for them. His asking for the red lentils was another reason for Esau being called Edom, not only because his skin tended toward red but also because of his asking for the lentils, whose color tends toward red.

25.16.0.en: Jacob took advantage of his brother's need for food and showed him his readiness to give him some of the lentils on condition that he sell him his birthright, because Esau was the one who came out first from his mother's womb, so he was the firstborn, and the birthright meant:

25.16.1.en: 1- That he would act for his father in his absence in the headship of the family.

25.16.2.en: 2- That he would receive a greater share of the inheritance at the death of the father.

25.16.3.en: 3- In the days of Jacob the head of the family used to offer sacrifices on behalf of his family, that is, he was the priest of the family, and in the absence of the father the firstborn acted for his father in this priestly work.

25.16.4.en: This conduct of Jacob was not sound, for he took advantage of his brother's need for food, and perhaps he also realized Esau's disregard for spiritual meanings, so he asked him to sell him his birthright.

25.17.0.en: Esau despised the spiritual blessing of the birthright and said, I am about to die of hunger, so what importance has the birthright? Give me food, for it is more important than the birthright. This conduct too was very wrong.

25.17.1.en: May you care for the spiritual opportunities that God has given you, such as a church near you, a priest before whom you can confess, and your ability to read the Holy Bible and the Agpeya so as to pray and meditate; indeed seize every spiritual opportunity, in a meeting or a trip, to cling to God and grow in His love, and do not sell these opportunities because of what you call the occupations of life.

25.18.0.en: Jacob asked Esau for a confirmation of the sale of his birthright, namely an oath, and he swore to him. Thus he sold the great birthright for the cheapest thing, a mere meal of lentils.

25.19.0.en: Jacob gave his brother bread and lentils, and he ate and enjoyed the food and did not care about the birthright; rather, by this conduct he despised it, so it was lost to him, and he lost the salvation of his soul and all his faith, and formed a people alien to the faith, the people of Edom.

26.0.0.en: A famine occurred a second time in the south of Canaan, other than the first famine that occurred in the days of Abraham, because of which he went down to the land of Egypt. So Isaac moved from Beer-lahai-roi to Gerar, which lies southeast of Gaza at a distance of 5 miles from it, and Abimelech reigned over it, which is a title of the kings of Gerar.

26.1.0.en: God warned him against going down to Egypt, and it seems that Isaac had prayed to God, who commanded him to remain in Canaan, the land that was promised to Abraham, and that He was able to provide for him and keep him in it, and he did not need to go down to Egypt, lest he be exposed to troubles as his father Abraham was. And He renewed His promise to him of blessing and many offspring in the land of Canaan for the sake of Abraham his father, so he obeyed and dwelt in Gerar.

26.1.1.en: Take care to cling to the righteous, the pious children of God, so that you receive their blessing in your life, and seek the intercession of the saints, so that God sees your love for them and blesses your life.

26.2.0.en: Isaac feared for himself that the people of the place would kill him and take from him his beautiful wife Rebekah, so he lied and said that she was his sister, and thus fell into the same sin as his father and did not learn from what had happened to him.

26.2.1.en: When you see the faults of others, do not hasten to condemn them, but rather take heed yourself lest you fall into the same faults, and know that we are all subject to weakness and exposed to sin, and the wise man is the one who learns from everyone, even from the wicked.

26.3.0.en: Isaac lived for a time in Gerar and pitched his tent near the palace of its king, who was called Abimelech, because it was the title of all the kings of Gerar, and he was probably a different king from the one in the days of Abraham. One day Abimelech looked out of the window of his palace and saw Isaac in his tent caressing Rebekah as a husband with his wife, so he understood that she was his wife and not his sister.

26.4.0.en: Abimelech summoned Isaac and confronted him with his lie about Rebekah, and he admitted it but justified his sin by his fear that the people of the place would kill him and take his wife. This sin is not only a lie but an evil suspicion of the people of Gerar, whose fear of doing evil appears, as will be shown in the following verses.

26.5.0.en: Abimelech reproached him for his lie, because by it he exposed one of the men of Gerar to falling into the sin of marrying Rebekah as his sister, and thus falling into evil without knowing it, so that through this sin of his all the people of Gerar would have become guilty, and all this because of Isaac's negligence and his lie.

26.6.0.en: Abimelech was firm, and despite Isaac's sin he issued an order in all his city declaring that Rebekah was Isaac's wife, so that no one should try to think of her as a wife for himself or come near her, and whoever tried that would be put to death.

26.7.0.en: Although Isaac had sinned by his lie, he was still distinguished by his faith in God, in which he was unique in all the world, so God forgave him after his repentance and his acceptance of Abimelech's rebuke of him. And when he sowed a piece of land in the region of Gerar, God gave him an abundance in his harvest beyond all imagination, a hundredfold the usual harvest of that time, and He also blessed his sheep so they multiplied greatly, and thus he became the richest man in Gerar and owned many servants. The people of Gerar envied him for his rapid greatness and his superiority over them.

26.8.0.en: The people of Gerar expressed their anger and envy toward Isaac by stopping up the wells that Abraham had dug when he lived among them, which are considered the property of his son Isaac. So that he should not use them and increase in his wealth, they stopped them up, that is, they kept water from them, hoping that he would leave them. And since he stayed and bore these bad actions, Abimelech was compelled to ask him to depart from them, because he had become mightier than they, and might gain mastery over them or rule them.

26.8.1.en: God's blessing surpasses all understanding, for although Isaac was a stranger and in weakness, God blessed him, so he became stronger than the original inhabitants. Trust in the power of God that is with you, and He will bless you more than all who are around you and give you peace, so that others will fear you.

26.9.0.en: Isaac the peaceable moved from Gerar to a region near it called the valley of Gerar, a few miles away from it.

26.10.0.en: Isaac was not troubled by the envy of the Philistines and their stopping up of the wells that Abraham had dug, which were considered his property, but positively, when he found some of these wells in the valley of Gerar, he began to dig them out, that is, to remove the earth and stones that the Philistines, the people of Gerar, had thrown into them. He knew their places, whether from his father or from the servants who had helped his father and were still alive, or from their sons.

26.11.0.en: Isaac found one of the wells that Abraham had dug and removed the earth that was on it, and it again gave water. When the Philistines found this, they rose against him and claimed ownership of this well, so he left it to them for the sake of peace and called this well Esek, that is, strife.

26.12.0.en: Isaac did not despair and continued his positive work, and a new well appeared from among the wells that Abraham had dug, but the Philistines also rose against him and claimed that this well was theirs, so Isaac gave it up also for the sake of peace and called this well Sitnah, that is, contention.

26.13.0.en: Isaac continued his search for water and was not hindered by the harassment of his wicked neighbors, and a third well appeared. Since God saw his perseverance and his love, He made the Philistines leave him alone and not seize this well, so Isaac rejoiced and called this well Rehoboth, that is, God has made room for us and enabled us to settle and be fruitful in the broad land, and he thanked God.

26.14.0.en: After this he moved to Beersheba, where Abraham had lived for a time after he had dug the well there and given the seven ewe lambs to Abimelech as proof of Abraham's ownership of it. God appeared to him in this blessed place and renewed to him the covenant of blessing, so that he would not be troubled by the harassment of the wicked and would trust that God was with him. So he built an altar and thanked God, and also dug a well in this place and settled there for a time, pasturing his flock.

26.15.0.en: Isaac, while living in the valley of Gerar, was surprised by the coming of Abimelech king of Gerar, with his friend or counselor Ahuzzath and Phichol the captain of his army. As we have said before, Abimelech is a title of the kings of Gerar and Phichol is a title of the commanders of the armies of Gerar, and they were probably different from the two who were in the days of Abraham.

26.16.0.en: Isaac wondered at their coming to him while they showed him love and friendliness, and asked them, how is it that you drove me away from you, and now you have come to me and speak to me with friendliness and love?

26.17.0.en: Abimelech and those with him acknowledged that the power of God and His blessing that was with Isaac made them fear him, and they came to him asking for a treaty of peace with him, so that he would not harm them.

26.18.0.en: Abimelech reminded him that although they had driven him away, they had not seized from him his wife or anything of his possessions ... and they asked for a covenant of peace and a treaty of peace between them because they felt that he was blessed by God.

26.19.0.en: Isaac's heart, broad with love, appeared when he made them a feast, that is, a table, and they ate and rested with him, and made a treaty of peace that neither would harm the other, and they swore to it and then departed from him.

26.19.1.en: Let your heart be broad with love toward everyone, even those who have wronged you, so that you forgive them and show them love and do not fear them, because God is with you and keeps you in all your ways, so you remain firm in your peace and your love.

26.20.0.en: Isaac's servants cleaned out the well that Abraham had dug in that place, or dug a new well, and it brought forth water, and they told Isaac their master, who rejoiced and confirmed the name of the place, calling it Beersheba (map 7).
